title: Primary Function of the System
learningObjectives: Identify the primary structural function of the seat-support arm.
student: What is the primary structural function of the seat-support arm?
instructor: The arm supports the seat and operator and transfers their load into the machine frame.

title: External Loading
learningObjectives: Identify the dominant external load acting on the support arm.
student: What is the dominant external loading acting on the support arm when an operator is seated?
instructor: The dominant load is the downward force from the operator and seat assembly.

title: Support and Restraint
learningObjectives: Relate the machine attachment to the motions it must resist.
student: How is the support arm connected to the machine structure, and what motions must that connection resist?
instructor: The arm is rigidly attached to the machine frame. The connection must resist vertical translation and rotation caused by the offset seat load.

title: Load Path
learningObjectives: Trace the occupant load through the support assembly.
student: Trace the dominant load path from the operator to the machine frame.
instructor: Operator → seat → seat mounting post → structural support arm → machine frame.

title: Effect of Seat Offset
learningObjectives: Explain how load offset affects bending demand.
student: For the same operator load, how would moving the seat farther away from the machine frame affect the bending demand in the support arm?
instructor: The bending demand increases because the load acts through a larger moment arm.

title: Critical Mechanical Response
learningObjectives: Identify the arm response relevant to structural strength.
student: What mechanical response in the support arm should be evaluated if structural strength under this load is the main concern?
instructor: The arm develops a bending moment that produces flexural normal stress. The largest tensile and compressive stresses occur at the outer fibers of the cross-section.

title: Relevant Cross-Sectional Geometry
learningObjectives: Identify the section dimensions that control bending resistance.
student: What general geometric features of the hollow rectangular arm would influence its resistance to bending?
instructor: The overall section depth, section width, and wall thickness influence the second moment of area. Increasing the section depth is especially effective because material located farther from the neutral axis contributes strongly to bending resistance.

title: Student-Generated Structural Idealization
learningObjectives: Convert the physical assembly into a mechanics model.
student:
Convert the real seat assembly into a simplified cantilever-beam model that preserves the dominant load path. Show the rigid machine attachment, the downward seat/occupant load, the horizontal load offset, and the hollow rectangular cross-section.

Student model / free-body diagram space:
instructor:
A correct idealization is a straight cantilever beam fixed to the machine frame, with a concentrated downward load applied through the seat-post line. The arm is modeled with a hollow rectangular cross-section.

Instructor note: The real image should guide the physical interpretation; the point labels and symbolic geometry are introduced only in the instructor reference model.

title: Modeling Assumptions
learningObjectives: State assumptions that bound the simplified bending model.
student: State the assumptions used in the simplified mechanics model.
instructor: Static loading; the arm is straight and prismatic; the occupant/seat load is treated as a concentrated force; material response is linear elastic; deformation is small; plane sections remain plane; arm and hardware self-weight are neglected unless included in the applied load; local weld, bolt, bracket, contact, stress-concentration, fatigue, impact, and dynamic-seat effects are excluded.

title: Mechanics Analysis Plan
learningObjectives: Organize the calculation sequence for maximum bending stress.
student: List the calculation sequence required to determine the maximum bending stress.
instructor: Determine the internal bending moment at the selected section, locate the centroidal neutral axis, calculate the second moment of area of the hollow rectangular section, determine the extreme-fiber distance, apply the flexure formula, and interpret the tension/compression sides and geometry sensitivity.

title: Boundary Condition
learningObjectives: Identify the reaction resultants available at the fixed support.
student: State the boundary condition at A and identify the reaction resultants available at the fixed support.
instructor: The fixed support prevents horizontal translation, vertical translation, and rotation. It can therefore provide horizontal reaction, vertical reaction, and a reaction moment. For the assigned vertical load case, the vertical reaction and moment are relevant.

title: Internal Shear and Bending Moment
learningObjectives: Determine internal shear and bending moment at section a-a.
student: Cut the arm at section a-a and determine the internal shear force and bending moment at the cut.
instructor: The internal shear-force magnitude is V = P = {{seat_V_lb}} lb. The bending-moment magnitude is M = Px = ({{seat_P}} lb)({{seat_x}} in.) = {{seat_M_lbin}} lb·in.

title: Neutral Axis
learningObjectives: Locate the centroidal neutral axis using symmetry.
student: Locate the centroidal neutral axis for bending about the horizontal centroidal axis.
instructor: Because the outer and inner rectangles are concentric and symmetric, the centroid lies at the geometric center and the neutral axis passes through the section at mid-height.

title: Second Moment of Area
learningObjectives: Calculate the second moment of area of the hollow rectangle.
student: Determine the second moment of area of section a-a about the horizontal centroidal axis.

title: Extreme-Fiber Distance
learningObjectives: Determine the distance from the neutral axis to an extreme fiber.
student: Determine the distance from the neutral axis to the extreme fiber.

title: Maximum Bending Stress
learningObjectives: Apply the flexure formula to determine maximum normal stress.
student: Determine the maximum normal bending stress at section a-a.

title: Stress Sense
learningObjectives: Identify the tensile and compressive extreme fibers.
student: Identify the tension and compression sides of the tube for the downward seat load.
instructor: The cantilever develops a hogging bending moment near the machine attachment. For the orientation shown, the {{seat_tension_fiber}} is in tension and the {{seat_compression_fiber}} is in compression. The magnitudes are equal because the section is symmetric about the neutral axis.

title: Geometry and Offset Sensitivity
learningObjectives: Compare geometric and loading changes that reduce bending stress.
student: Which change would most effectively reduce the bending stress: increasing section height, increasing section width, or reducing the seat offset? Explain.
instructor: Increasing section height is very effective because the second moment of area depends strongly on section depth. Reducing the seat offset also directly reduces the bending moment because M = Px. Increasing the section width increases I more nearly linearly.

title: Engineering Assessment
learningObjectives: Identify the critical region and recommend a mechanics-based change.
student: Based on the calculated stress and mechanics relationships, identify the critical region of the support arm and recommend one practical mechanics-based change that would reduce bending demand.
